page.content:
The pattern of Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear, and Othello: a fall that takes a state with it.

How Shakespearean tragedy connects

  • Work: Hamlet — Hamlet is a central Shakespearean tragedy.
  • Work: Macbeth — Macbeth is a central Shakespearean tragedy.
  • Work: King Lear — King Lear is a central Shakespearean tragedy.
  • Work: Othello — Othello is a central Shakespearean tragedy.
  • Work: Romeo and Juliet — Romeo and Juliet is an early Shakespearean tragedy of the two houses.

What is Shakespearean tragedy?

Shakespearean tragedy is the late-Elizabethan and Jacobean form in which a prince, thane, king, or general — Hamlet, Macbeth, Lear, Othello — destroys a household or a kingdom from the inside.

Key threads lead to Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear, Othello and Romeo and Juliet.
